patch.description: Theorems stating, for every metric in a broad class, how much negative energy a 'warp' or 'propellantless' spacetime needs, or how much positive mass a positive-energy version must carry. Superluminal bubbles must violate the null energy condition. The only published positive-energy subluminal shell (Fuchs et al. 2024) carries 2.365 Jupiter masses within a 10-20 m shell for a 0.02c internal shift; no theorem yet fixes the minimum mass of such shells. Sharp constants for the negative-energy cases are now being computed.
patch.status_oct2026: Human literature, mostly T5: generic warp drives violate the null energy condition (Santiago-Schuster-Visser, arXiv 2105.03079, May 2021), which answered the 2020-21 positive-energy claims of Lentz, Bobrick-Martire and Fell-Heisenberg within months; a direct computation showing negative Eulerian energy density and errors in Lentz's construction followed in Nov 2025 (arXiv 2511.18251). A subluminal warp satisfies all energy conditions only by adding a matter shell with positive ADM mass (Fuchs et al., arXiv 2405.02709, 2024: 4.49e27 kg, about 2.4 Jupiter masses, inner radius 10 m). New no-go theorems and classification (arXiv 2602.16495, Feb 2026); exact minimum Eulerian negative energy for Natario drives, E_min ~ v^2 R^4/(4 Delta^3) (arXiv 2609.36211, Sep 28 2026, unrefereed). The spacetime positive mass theorem (zero ADM mass with dominant energy forces flat spacetime) is established. Family 260 (T1) extends Penrose mass-area bounds to data with arbitrary momentum, a marginal addition.
patch.why: Ceilings act within months (fc-position-1). (1) By the Natario result (an unrefereed human preprint, Sep 28 2026), halving the bubble wall thickness multiplies the negative energy needed 8x and doubling the bubble radius multiplies it 16x; for R/Delta = 100 the sharp bound is 2,500x the older v^2R^2/Delta estimate. (2) Penrose-type mass bounds (family 260 for moving data, conditional on T1) apply only to data containing trapped surfaces, that is, black holes, which warp shells avoid: the Fuchs et al. shell has a Schwarzschild radius of about 6.7 m, inside its 10 m inner radius, so it has no trapped surface and these bounds do not bind any published design. (3) Any 'zero-mass' warp metric that is not flat must violate the dominant energy condition (positive mass rigidity). An exponentially improving model can extend these to every published warp class with sharp constants, and could prove a minimum mass for positive-energy shells, which is cognitive work only. Outside teams must pose the warp-class questions, so the node follows public access (cap-research-math-public).

patch.description: Quantum energy inequalities cap how much negative energy a quantum field can hold and for how long. They are proven for free fields on arbitrary globally hyperbolic spacetimes (Fewster 2000) and for one interacting two-dimensional model (the massive Ising model, 2013); interacting four-dimensional theories remain open. A QEI, or a proven absence of one, for an interacting 4D theory (at least perturbatively) would close the remaining 'quantum loophole' that warp and wormhole proposals point to.
patch.status_oct2026: Worldline QEIs for free scalar fields on arbitrary globally hyperbolic spacetimes with Hadamard states (Fewster, arXiv gr-qc/9910060, 2000); the first QEI for an interacting theory with nontrivial S-matrix, the massive Ising model in two dimensions (Bostelmann-Cadamuro-Fewster, arXiv 1304.7682, 2013); quantum inequalities applied to Alcubierre walls in 1997 give walls a few hundred Planck lengths thick and an unattainable total energy (Pfenning-Ford, arXiv gr-qc/9702026, using flat-space inequalities on short sampling times). Averaged null energy condition proven for flat-space QFT (2016-17, general). Open: interacting 4D theories. Not in the catalog.

patch.status_oct2026: Second-order calculations exist only for quasicircular orbits around non-spinning (Schwarzschild) black holes (arXiv 2112.12265; effective-source paper arXiv 2508.00087, 2025); a June 2026 paper states 'these calculations have only been attempted for the simplest case of circular orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime' and demonstrates a numerical-relativity route in Kerr for a scalar charge (arXiv 2606.04998); Lorenz-gauge elliptic methods in progress (arXiv 2608.07934, Aug 2026). Adiabatic-order Kerr waveforms for equatorial orbits exist in the FastEMRIWaveforms framework (Phys. Rev. D, Apr 2025); interpolation errors in such fast models are themselves a bias source (PRD, Mar 2026). The second-order formalism (puncture field, two-timescale field equations) was extended to eccentric Schwarzschild orbits (Wei, Zhu, Zhang, Mei, PRD 112, 064048, 2025; arXiv 2504.09640); waveforms still exist only for quasicircular Schwarzschild.
patch.why: The phase expands as phi = phi_0/epsilon + phi_1 + O(epsilon) with mass ratio epsilon ~1e-5 to 1e-6; adiabatic waveforms carry only phi_0, and the O(1) post-adiabatic term phi_1 needs second-order self-force (general). Part of what remains is research, not labor: metric reconstruction and gauge choice at second order in Kerr are open (the separable Teukolsky machinery does not carry over cleanly, which is why groups are trying numerical-relativity and Lorenz-gauge elliptic routes), and first-order adiabatic Kerr inputs exist only for equatorial orbits. The rest is expert labor (renormalized sources, mode coupling, eccentric and inclined orbits) by a few dozen specialists, the class where on-demand AI applied math (P1) acts first, followed by a compute campaign: second-order sources over a 4-D grid (spin, p, e, inclination) with mode coupling that grows quadratically in the number of modes, plus agreement between independent codes. Chain (S2): cap-applied-math 2027 -> Kerr second-order formalism and gauge 2028 -> eccentric and inclined sources and codes 2029 -> compute and cross-code validation, results 2030. That is roughly three to five years ahead of a pre-AI path that aimed to finish before the 2035 launch (analyst judgment, no source). In S3 cognition is near-free from 2029, but compute and independent-code validation still bind, so S3 is a year earlier and still Medium. Bands are judgments.

patch.description: LISA will see massive black-hole mergers at signal-to-noise ratios in the hundreds to thousands, where waveform error dominates the error budget. Simulations need mismatches near 1e-6 (indistinguishability scales as ~1/(2 SNR^2), general) at mass ratios above 10 and spins near 0.9, versus a median resolution difference of ~4e-4 today.
patch.status_oct2026: SXS third catalog (CQG, Oct 2025; arXiv 2505.13378): 3,756 configurations at about 480 million core-hours in total; median resolution difference 4e-4; precessing runs cover q<=8 and |chi|<=0.8, plus over 100 runs between q=8 and q=20 (mostly with spin only on the larger hole); longest run 148 orbits. Mismatch reaches ~1e-1 for ~180-orbit runs (arXiv 2502.14025). Bias studies show neglected harmonics and eccentricity bias LISA parameters (arXiv 2502.12237, 2602.09088, 2601.07739). GPU code generation for NR emerging (arXiv 2501.14030; up to 16x single-precision speedups for an elliptic solver).

patch.title: Coronal heating: an AI-built model passes a blind test
patch.description: A predictive model of coronal heating and solar-wind acceleration, built by AI from Parker Solar Probe, Solar Orbiter and PUNCH data, makes a discriminating quantitative prediction (one on which the leading mechanisms, waves and turbulence versus small-scale reconnection and switchbacks, disagree) that a later encounter confirms. This is the measurable step; community consensus that the problem is settled would come later.
patch.why: One of the few open physics problems where the data largely exist and theory-building is the bottleneck, so S2/S3 physics-theory capability could matter, and several perihelia a year give repeated chances to test. The band can be no better than its hard prerequisite (cap-physics-theory, S2 Medium), and a model must be built and then tested against a later encounter, so S2 is Low and S3 Medium; S1 Speculative. Heliospheric tomography helps but is not required: global white-light density barely constrains kinetic-scale heating. A confirmed mechanism would shape what the next heliophysics missions measure (high-cadence spectroscopy versus in-situ kinetic plasma). Bands are judgments.

patch.title: Laser-propelled gram-scale sail demonstrated
patch.description: Demonstration of stable laser-driven propulsion of a gram-scale sail over meters or more, in a ground vacuum facility or in free (suborbital or orbital) flight. Force or torque measurements on smaller membranes count toward science-lightsail-stability, not here.
patch.why: By F = 2P/c, accelerating 1 g at 1 m/s^2 takes about 150 kW of reflected laser power (a 10 kW-class laser gives about 0.07 m/s^2), plus a sail that survives the absorbed heat and stays on the beam. Chain: stability designs 2028 (S2) -> laboratory force and torque validation 2029-30 -> a sponsor funds a high-power propulsion facility and gram-scale sails -> demonstration. No sponsor or facility is named as of Oct 2026, and capital compresses at most 1.3-1.5x even in S3, so the demonstration is after 2031 in every scenario (Speculative; judgment).

add_nodes.description: A philanthropically or commercially funded space telescope of 1 m aperture class or larger, built outside agency selection and appropriations, returns science data by 2031. It qualifies 'no observatory flies sooner': outside agency selection and appropriations, the physical clock is the only clock. A second, AI-native private observatory started in 2028 and flying by 2031 would need an unannounced funder and is not counted.

add_nodes.title: Science spacecraft downlink answers with certified error bounds
add_nodes.description: A science mission (smallsat, hosted payload or Explorer-class; new, or by software upload to an operating spacecraft) runs onboard inference that turns raw instrument data into science products (event detections, classifications, spectral fits, compressed fields) with certified error bounds (stated false-negative and distortion rates) that its science team accepts in place of raw data for a stated share of its downlink, and retargets observations on those products. It cannot recover information the photons never carried; the gain is selection and compression of what is recorded.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: Onboard autonomy for science is not new: EO-1's Autonomous Sciencecraft Experiment detected events and retargeted from 2004 (general); AEGIS selects rover targets onboard Curiosity and Perseverance (general); ESA's Phi-sat-2 (launched Aug 2024) runs onboard AI applications including image compression and cloud detection (ESA). Missing are certified error bounds that let a science team discard raw data; most science instruments still downlink raw or losslessly compressed data (general).
add_nodes.why: Two curves combine: onboard compute is becoming routine (COTS AI chips in orbit, materials-cots-orbital-compute-ops, S2 2028) and AI applied math makes instrument-specific error analysis cheap. Chain (S2): cap-applied-math 2027 -> error-bounded detection and compression for a specific instrument 2028 -> software upload to an operating mission or a rideshare smallsat (12-18 month lag ladder for derivative payloads) -> operating with a stated downlink saving in 2029. It attacks downlink, part of the domain's dominant data-supply bottleneck (research/science.json). S2 Medium because science teams are conservative about discarding raw data and certification is the novelty, not the inference; S3 High because cognition is near-free from 2029 and one mission (a university smallsat is enough) clears the bar with two years of slack; S1 Low because applied math reaches outside teams only in 2029. S3 equals S2 through 2028. Bands are judgments.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Distribution-free error bounds (conformal prediction, lossy-compression bounds) already exist, so the mathematics is not the barrier; and optical downlinks may relieve the bottleneck faster than onboard inference.
add_nodes.signpost: A science mission team publishes onboard-derived products with certified error bounds and reports the share of downlink saved.

patch.thesis: If AI can do the theory, inference and instrument mathematics behind missions, science return per dollar rises from existing archives by 2028 and big-telescope design work gets cheaper. Flight dates do not move: LISA still launches in 2035, BHEX cannot fly before about 2032, and HWO moves at the pace of appropriations (FY2027 request: $5M, down from $150M). The one lane where an observatory can fly sooner is privately funded, such as Schmidt Sciences' 3 m Lazuli (target 2028), and there the physical clock, not AI, sets the date. Warp drives get sharper no-go theorems, not engines.
